rows.speaker: ابن القيم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim cites a Prophetic report in the Musnad and elsewhere describing hearts as God's vessels on earth, with the most beloved firm, tender, and pure.
rows.anchor: قال العلامه الشمس ابن القيم فى شفاء العليل ما نصه وفى المسند وغيره عن النبى ( صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ) القلوب انية الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو عنبسة الخولاني
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī transmits from Abū ʿAnbasa al-Khawlānī a raised report that righteous servants' hearts are God's earthly vessels and the most beloved are soft and tender; Baqiyya ibn al-Walīd is a mudallis but explicitly transmits it.
rows.anchor: ورى الطبرانى من حديث أبى عنبسة الخولانى رفعه ان لله تعالى انية من الأرض وانية ربكم قلوب عباده الصالحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Combining the two reports yields four traits of the dearest heart: softness accepts truth, firmness preserves it, and tenderness and purity enable its vision.
rows.anchor: ويعلم من مجموع الحديثين أربع صفات للقلب الأحب اليه تعالى اللين وهو لقبول الحق والصلابة وهى لحفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's establishment over the Throne in the attribute of the All-Merciful rather than the Merciful signals that everyone receives a share of His expansive mercy.
rows.anchor: واستواؤه تعالى على العرش بصفة الرحمانية دون الرحيمة للاشارة إلى أن لكل أحد نصيبا من واسع رحمته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation calls the secret something latent in the heart like fire in damp wood, stirred into view by will; the more hidden thing lies within it.
rows.anchor: قيل : السر أمر كامن فى القلب كمون النار فى الشجر الرطب حيث تثيره الأرادة لا يطلع عليه الملك

rows.speaker: بعض الصوفية
rows.claim: Some Sufis define the secret as a subtle center between heart and spirit, the seat of spiritual mysteries, and the hidden as between spirit and divine presence, where divine lights descend.
rows.anchor: وعند بعض الصوفية السر لطيفه بين القلب والروح وهو معدن الأسرار الروحانية والخفى لطيفة بين الروح والحضرة الالهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although some infer that loud remembrance is not prescribed, al-Alūsī says it is prescribed with its conditions; absent a text preferring volume or concealment, the better mode varies by person, circumstance, and time.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل بعض الناس بهذه الآية على عدم مشروعية الجهر بالذكر والحق أنه مشروع بشرطه

rows.speaker: إبراهيم الكوراني
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Kūrānī says the fire was a locus of divine manifestation, fitting the wisdom that it was what Moses sought; he supports this with an Ibn ʿAbbās report to be cited at 27:8.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ إبراهيم الكورانى عليه الرحمة فى تنبيه العقول : أن تلك النار كانت مجلى الله عز وجل وتجليه سبحانه فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Removing the sandals symbolizes turning away from worldly and otherworldly concerns, letting the heart be wholly absorbed in knowing God and attending to nothing else.
rows.anchor: فاخلع نعليكاترك الالتفات إلى الدنيا والاخرة وسر مستغرق القلب بالكلية فى معرفة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the sandals the two premises of a proof; Moses is told to leave inference behind because he is in the valley of direct knowledge of God.
rows.anchor: وقيل : النعلان إشارة إلى المقدمتين اللتين يتركب منهما الدليل لانهما يتوصل بهما العقل إلى المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sacred valley Ṭuwā is the valley of God's holy majesty and the transcendence of His might.
rows.anchor: انك بالوادى المقدس طوى وهو وادى قدس جلال الله تعالى وتنزه عزته عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to worship comes first to honor servitude; prayer follows as a sign of servitude and an ascent to the holy presence.
rows.anchor: قدم هذا الأمر للاشارة إلى عظم شرف العبودية وثنى بقوله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asks about the object in Moses' hand to comfort him: after being awed by divine speech, he can answer an easy question correctly and recover his composure.
rows.anchor: ايناس منه تعالى له عليه السلام فانه عليه السلام دهش لما تكلم سبحانه معه بما يتعلق بالالوهية فسأله عن شئ بيده

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported analogy says that after death the believer is similarly asked about the faith held in worldly life; recalling it removes the awe of arriving in God's presence.
rows.anchor: قيل وكذلك يعامل المؤمن بعد موته وذلك أنه إذا مات وصل إلى حضرة ذى الجلال فيعتريه ما يعتريه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says God first showed Moses perfect divinity, then human limitation: asking about the staff's uses showed how even a present object exceeds what reason can know without divine guidance.
rows.anchor: لما عرفه كمال الالوهية اراد أن يعرفه نقصان البشرية فسأله عن منافع العصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff becoming a moving serpent signals the manifestation of divine majesty; Moses' fear reflects perfected knowledge because he did not feel secure from God's plan.
rows.anchor: فيه إشارة إلى ظهور اثر الجلال ولذلك خاف موسى عليه السلام فقال سبحانه خذها ولا تخف فهذا الخوف من كمال المعرفة

rows.speaker: بعض الآثار
rows.claim: An unattributed report says God told Moses not to feel secure from His plan until he had crossed the Sirat.
rows.anchor: وفى بعض الآثار يا موسى لا تامن مكرى حتى تجوز الصراط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī rejects the suggestion that Moses feared losing the staff's listed benefits, since it misjudges Moses' spiritual station.
rows.anchor: كان خوفه من فوات المنافع المعدودة ولذا علل النهى بقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He likewise rejects the claim that Moses fled because he had not attained the station of fleeing to God, saying this imputes ignorance of Moses' rank.
rows.anchor: وكذا ما قيل : أنه لما رأى الأمر الهائل فر حيث لم يبلغ مقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects as another misunderstanding the speculation that Moses' encounter made him conceited, so God reminded him of his continuing ontological deficiency and human nature.
rows.anchor: ما قيل : أيضا لعله لما حصل له مقام المكالمة بقى فى قلبه عجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Victory and steadfastness come from God alone.
rows.anchor: وما النصر والتثبيت إلا من عند الله تعالى وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' bodily sign follows the staff, an external sign, echoing the promise that God will show signs on the horizons and within people themselves.
rows.anchor: اراد سبحانه أن يريه آية نفسية بعد أن اراه عليه السلام آية إفاقية كما قال سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff and hand each became a brilliant proof: lifeless matter turned to an animal, while dense matter became luminous and subtle.
rows.anchor: حصل فى كل منهما برهان باهر ومعجز قاهر فصار أحدهما وهو الجماد حيوانا والأخر وهو الكثيف نورانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God looks at a servant's heart 360 times each day, the inert, dark heart can likewise turn living and radiant.
rows.anchor: ينظر فى كل يوم ثلثمائة وستين نظرة إلى قلب العبد فاى عجب أن ينقلب قلبه الجامد المظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As Moses' right hand readied the staff for life, the believer's heart, held between God's fingers, can be prepared for life.
rows.anchor: العصا قد استعدت بيمن يمين موسى عليه السلام للحياة وصارت حية فكيف لا يستعد قلب المؤمن الذى هو بين اصبعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff swallowed the sorcerers' magic at one sign; repeated divine regard can make a believer's heart swallow the evil-commanding soul's magic.
rows.anchor: العصا باشارة واحدة صارت بحيث ابتلعت سحر السحرة فقلب المؤمن أولى أن يصير بمدد نظر الرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Removing sandals signifies emptying the conscience of distractions; what follows signifies adorning it and acquiring what was absent.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى التخلية وتطهير لوح الضمير من الاغيار وما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address maps knowledge of God to the beginning, worship and prayer to the middle and bodily and spiritual practice, and the coming Hour to knowledge of the return.
rows.anchor: واشار سبحانه إلى علم المبدأ بقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening with divine choice conveys utmost kindness and the closing warning conveys overpowering severity, teaching that mercy precedes wrath and the servant must walk between hope and fear.
rows.anchor: افتتح الخطاب بقوله عز قائلا ( وانا اخترتك ) وهو غاية اللطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feet enable escape and hands pursuit; surrendering sandals and staff teaches that self-directed seeking and fleeing impede complete absorption in gnosis, even for a great prophet.
rows.anchor: موسى عليه السلام كان في رجله شئ وهو النعل وفى يده شئ وهو العصا وارجل الة الهرب واليد الة الطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Direct divine speech to Moses does not establish his superiority over Muhammad: God also addressed Muhammad directly on the Night Journey, and did so unveiled and with a vision not granted Moses.
rows.anchor: والجواب أنه تعالى شأنه قد خاطب نبينا ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) أيضا بلا واسطة ليلة المعراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī contrasts Muhammad's report that his sight neither swerved nor transgressed with Moses' simple answer about his staff, seeing a clear difference in their ranks.
rows.anchor: وانظر إلى الفرق بين قوله تعالى عن نبينا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some add that Moses leaned on his staff while Muhammad relied on God's grace, citing Muhammad's assurance that God suffices him and his believing followers.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن في الآيات ما يشعر بالفرق بينهما أيضا عليهما الصلاة والسلام من وجه أخر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Moses first named his own needs and then his flock, whereas Muhammad cared only for his community, praying for their guidance; at judgment Moses says 'myself' and Muhammad 'my community.'
rows.anchor: بدأ بمصالح نفسه فى قوله : ( أتوكأ عليها ) ثم مصالح رعيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī warns readers not to emulate these comparisons, which he says have only a very slight basis; he quoted them to prevent being impressed by them.
rows.anchor: ولعمرى أنه لاينبغى أن يقتدى به فى مثل هذا الكلام كما لايخفى على ذوى الافهام

rows.speaker: قال بعض الناس
rows.claim: An interpretation catalogs ten lights—God, Messenger, scripture, faith, justice, moon, day, proofs, prophets, and gnosis—and maps Moses' first five requests to divine majesty, prophetic character, obedience to revelation, faith and certainty, and insight into divine justice.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الناس : أنه تعالى ذكر عشرة أشياء ووصفها بالنور الأول ذاته

rows.speaker: قال بعض الناس
rows.claim: The sixth request moves from the lights of sun and moon to the lights of divine majesty, as Abraham did.
rows.anchor: وسادسا رب اشرح لى صدرى بالانتقال من نور شمسك وقمرك إلى انوار جلال عوتك كما فعله إبراهيم

rows.speaker: قال بعض الناس
rows.claim: The seventh asks to move from observing day and night to contemplating the day of divine favor and night of divine overpowering.
rows.anchor: وسابعا رب اشرح لى صدرى من مطالعة نهارك وليلك إلى مطالعة نهار فضلك وليل قهرك

rows.speaker: قال بعض الناس
rows.claim: The eighth asks to perceive the totality of God's signs and the points of His proofs in earth and heavens.
rows.anchor: وثامنا رب اشرح لى صدرى بالاطلاع على مجاميع اياتك ومعاقد بيناتك فى ارضك وسمواتك

rows.speaker: قال بعض الناس
rows.claim: The ninth asks Moses to be a worthy successor to earlier prophets and imitate their submission to the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: وتاسعا رب اشرح لى صدرى فى أن اكون خلف صدق للانبياء المتقدمين ومشابها لهم فى الأنقياد

rows.speaker: قال بعض الناس
rows.claim: The tenth asks for faith's lamp to become like the niche containing a lamp.
rows.anchor: وعاشرا رب اشرح لى صدرى بأن يجعل سراج الايمان كالمشكاة التى فيها المصباح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī observes that most items in the ten-part interpretation entail or duplicate one another.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى ما بين اكثر ما ذكر من التلازم واغناء بعضه عن بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another allegory defines an expanded chest as kindling light in the heart until it becomes a lamp.
rows.anchor: وقال ايضا : أن شرح الصدر عبارة عن ايقاد النور فى القلب حتى يصير كالسراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lamp's seven necessities symbolize striving, humble supplication, resisting desire, repentance, patience, gratitude, and contentment with God's decree.
rows.anchor: فالزند زند المجاهدة والذين جاهدوا فينا والحجر حجر التضرع ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once these spiritual tools are ready, one should not rely on them but seek the goal from God; Moses then hears that his request is granted.
rows.anchor: ثم إذا صلحت هذه الأدوات فلا تعول عليها بل ينبغى أن تطلب المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritual knowledge surpasses corporeal sunlight because clouds veil the sun, while the sun of gnosis is not veiled by the seven heavens.
rows.anchor: الأول أن الشمس يحجبها الغيم وشمس المعرفة لا تحجبها السموات السبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The physical sun sets at night, but the sun of gnosis never sets; night worship is especially powerful, and the cited verses celebrate dawn devotion and the Night Journey.
rows.anchor: الثانى الشمس تغيب ليلا وشمس المعرفة لا تغيب ليلا إن ناشئة الليل هى أشد وطئا وأقوم قيلا

rows.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
rows.claim: A poem calls night a veil for lovers and wishes its hours would last, illustrating the enduring night of spiritual intimacy.
rows.anchor: الليل للعاشقين ستر يا ليت أوقاته تدوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The physical sun will end when rolled up, whereas gnosis does not perish: its root is firm and it bears heavenly fruit, ending in peace from the Merciful.
rows.anchor: الثالث الشمس تفنى إذا الشمس كورت والمعرفه لا تفنى أصلها ثابت وفرعها فى السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sunlight is eclipsed by the moon, but knowledge of God's oneness reaches the limbs only when joined to the moon of prophethood, the testimony that Muhammad is His messenger.
rows.anchor: الرابع الشمس إذا قابلها القمر انكسفت وشمس المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun darkens faces, while gnosis brightens faces on the Day when faces become bright.
rows.anchor: الخامس الشمس تسود الوجه والمعرفة تبيض الوجوه يوم تبيض وجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun causes a headache, while gnosis ascends.
rows.anchor: السادس الشمس تصدع والمعرفة تصعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun burns, while gnosis prevents burning; a saying tells the believer that his light has extinguished the flames.
rows.anchor: السابع الشمس تحرق والمعرفة يمنع من الاحراق جز يا مؤمن فقد أطفأ نورك لهبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun benefits people in this life, but gnosis benefits in both lives, bringing a good life and the best reward.
rows.anchor: الثامن الشمس منفعتها فى الدنيا والمعرفة منفعتها فى الدارين فلنحيينه حياة طيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun appears above but signifies what is below; divine gnoses have the reverse relation between outward form and inward meaning.
rows.anchor: التاسع الشمس فوقانية الصورة تحتانية المعنى والمعارف الالهية بالعكس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun shines on friend and enemy alike, whereas gnosis is acquired only by God's friend.
rows.anchor: العاشر الشمس تقع على الولى والعدو والمعرفة لا تحصل إلا للولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun reveals creatures' states, whereas gnosis carries the heart to the Creator.
rows.anchor: الحادى عشر الشمس تعرف احوال الخلق والمعرفة توصل القلب إلى الخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses begins by asking for an expanded chest because it is the first spiritual station and nobler than the highest corporeal station; its sign is turning from delusion toward the eternal abode.
rows.anchor: ولما كان شرح الصدر الذى هو أول مراتب الروحانيات اشرف من اعلى مراتب الجسمانيات بدأ موسى عليه السلام بطلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chest resembles a fortress: detachment from delusion forms its moat and desire for eternity its wall, keeping Satan's armies of blameworthy traits from the heart.
rows.anchor: وشبهوا الصدر بقلعة وجعلوا الأول كالخندق لها والثانى كالسور فمتى كان الخندق عظيما والسور محكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sufi terminology assigns Islam to the chest, faith to the heart, witnessing to the inner heart, and divine unity to the innermost intellect.
rows.anchor: وفرقوا بين الصدر والقلب والفؤاد واللب بأن الصدر مقر الاسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks for chest rather than heart because chest expansion entails heart expansion, serves as its prelude, and the generous Lord grants the result when the petitioner asks for its prerequisite.
rows.anchor: وإنما سأل موسى عليه السلام شرح الصدر دون القلب لأن انشراح الصدر يستلزم انشراح القلب دون العكس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' restraint in asking only for the lesser degree exemplifies proper etiquette and earns the requested end; when he boldly asked to see God, he was told he would not see Him.
rows.anchor: فقيل : ( قد أوتيت سؤلك يا موسى )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between Moses asking his Lord to expand his chest and Muhammad being told that God expanded his chest makes Moses the seeker and Muhammad the sought one.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى ما بين قول موسى عليه السلام لربه عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī further contrasts Moses seeking a benefit for himself with Muhammad, who answered the greeting in the divine presence by including himself and God's righteous servants.
rows.anchor: ويزيد الفرق ظهورا أن موسى عليه السلام فى الحضرة الالهية طلب لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses seeks the ability to express divine realities clearly because the subject is difficult to explain and listeners can stumble over obscure formulations.
rows.anchor: كأنه عليه السلام طلب قدرة التعبير عن الحقائق الالهية بعبارة واضحة فان المطلب وعر لا يكاد توجد له عبارة تسهله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says Moses asked to release his shyness at addressing God's enemy with the tongue he had used to address God.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أنه عليه السلام سأل حل عقدة الحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Perhaps Moses means speech that guides people; gnostics seek to speak with others only when it benefits their guidance.
rows.anchor: ولعله أراد من القول المضاف القول الذى به ارشاد للعباد فان همة العارفين لا تطلب النطق والمكالمة مع الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech is a great gift, as the Qur'an links the Merciful's teaching, human creation, and instruction in expression.
rows.anchor: نعم النطق من حيث هو فضيلة عظيمة وموهبة جسيمة ولهذا قال سبحانه

rows.speaker: على
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī quotes three sayings attributed to ʿAlī: without a tongue a person is only an image or an unattended beast; a person is hidden beneath his tongue; and a person is defined by his heart and tongue.
rows.anchor: وعن على كرم الله تعالى وجهه ما الانسان لولا اللسان إلا صورة مصورة أو بهيمة مهملة

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr's verse says a young man's tongue and heart are each half of him, leaving only flesh and blood.
rows.anchor: وقال زهير : لسان الفتى نصف ونصف فؤاده فلم يبق إلا صورة اللحم والدم

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: Some praise silence as safer, citing the saying that a person dies from a slip of the tongue but not a slip of the foot, and an aphorism warning one to guard one's mouth.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من مدح الصمت لأنه اسلم يموت الفتى من عثرة بلسانه وليس يموت المرء من عثرة الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī says silence is not inherently virtuous because it is an absence; speech is virtuous in itself but may become blameworthy for contingent reasons, so the Prophet praised saying good or remaining safely silent.
rows.anchor: والانصاف أن الصمت فى نفسه ليس بفضيلة لأنه أمر عدمى والمنطق فى نفسه فضيلة لكن قد يصير رذيلة لاسباب عرضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses does not ask for perfect eloquence because it belongs to Muhammad, the most eloquent speaker of Arabic.
rows.anchor: وذكر فى وجه عدم طلبه عليه السلام الفصاحة الكاملة انها نصيب الحبيب عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' request for Aaron as minister indicates that cooperation in religion is virtuous and characteristic of the messengers.
rows.anchor: فيه إشارة إلى فضيلة التعاون فى الدين فانه من أخلاق المرسلين عليهم صلوات الله تعالى وسلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ministry is praiseworthy when the minister plants deeds he will not regret at the harvest before the King of kings.
rows.anchor: والوزارة المتعارفة بين الناس ممدوحة إن زرع الوزير فى ارضها ما لا يندم عليه وقت حصاده بين يدى ملك الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request also illustrates the virtue of interceding for deserving people, especially relatives.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة أيضا إلى فضيلة التوسط بالخير للمستحقين لا سيما إذا كانوا من ذوى القرابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Withholding help from those entitled to it is unjust.
rows.anchor: ومن منع المستوجبين فقد ظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' precedence over his older brother Aaron shows that merit does not depend on age; God grants favor to whom He wills.
rows.anchor: وفى تقديم موسى عليه السلام مع أنه أصغر سنا على هرون عليه السلام مع أنه الأكبر دليل على أن الفضل غير تابع للسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ending the supplication by affirming God's watchfulness is exemplary etiquette and a powerful means of approach, and it helps bring the prayer's answer.
rows.anchor: فى ختم الأدعية بذلك من حسن الأدب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder of God's earlier favor strengthens Moses' certainty and suggests that God does not reject someone after accepting him or withhold favor after kindness; a saying adds that faith, once in the heart, is safe from loss.
rows.anchor: تذكير له عليه السلام بما يزيد إيقانه وفيه إشارة إلى أنه تعالى لا يرد بعد القبول ولا يحرم بعد الأحسان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A saying drawn from this passage claims that once faith enters the heart it is secure from being stripped away, and those who turn back do so only along the road.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا قيل : إذا دخل الأيمان القلب آمن السلب وما رجع من رجع إلا من الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's choosing Moses for Himself means singling him out through spiritual detachment so nothing distracts him from God.
rows.anchor: افردتك لى بالتجريد فلا يشغلك عنى شئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' years in Midian refer to his service to Shuʿayb; God trained him through a messenger's company so he would acquire prophetic manners and etiquette. Sufi teaching values good company and warns against bad company.
rows.anchor: أشير بذلك إلى خدمته لشعيب عليه السلام وذلك تربية منه تعالى له بصحبة المرسلين ليكون متخلقا بأخلاقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses arrived at the appointed time of full readiness and prophetic commissioning, which the author identifies as age forty.
rows.anchor: وذلك زمان كمال الاستعداد ووقت بعثة الأنبياء عليهم السلام وهو زمن بلوغهم أربعين سنه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A warning says anyone who reaches forty without good outweighing evil should mourn and prepare for the Fire.
rows.anchor: ومن بلغ الأربعين ولم يغلب خيره على شره فلينح على نفسه وليتجهز إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary explains Pharaoh's transgression as intoxication from divine overpowering, the attribute of the commanding soul; intoxication of divine gentleness belongs to the spirit and produces ecstatic utterances and claims of selfhood.
rows.anchor: جاوز الحد فى المعصية حتى ادعى الربوبية وذلك أثر سكر القهر الذى هو وصف النفس الأمارة ويقابله سكر اللطف وهو وصف الروح

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: Some excuse the ecstatic utterance of an intoxicated mystic such as al-Ḥallāj, while those jealous for God say there is no difference between him and Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: قالوا : وصاحبه معذور وإلا لم يكن فرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gentle-speech instruction teaches the proper way to guide others.
rows.anchor: فيه إشارة إلى تعليم كيفية الأرشاد

rows.speaker: النهرجوري
rows.claim: Al-Nahrjūrī says Moses was commanded to speak gently because Pharaoh had treated him well at the beginning of his life.
rows.anchor: وقال النهر جورى : أن الأمر بذلك لأنه احسن إلى موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bodies are cages for the soul's nightingales; spirits belong to the realm of dominion and have illuminated these bodily forms.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى الهياكل واقفاص بلابل الأرواح وإلا فالأرواح أنفسها من عالم الملكوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī says he has mostly left aside interpreters' readings of this story and its verses as references to the inner self, retaining only a little of that approach.
rows.anchor: وقد تأول بعض أهل التأويل هذه القصة والآيات على ما فى الأنفس وهو مشرب قد تركناه إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text omits the mention of Moses arriving because his arrival is already established and needs no explicit statement.
rows.anchor: للايذان أنه أمر محقق غنى عن التصريح به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is a fresh explanatory start answering the implicit question of what Moses did when Pharaoh assembled the sorcerers; Moses addresses them as a warning.
rows.anchor: والجملة مستانفة استئنافا بيانيا كأنه قيل : فماذا صنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses warns them not to claim that the signs soon shown through him are magic, as Pharaoh had done.
rows.anchor: بأن تدعوا إياته التى ستظهر على يدى سحرا كما فعل فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means that God will utterly destroy them with a terrible punishment beyond measure.
rows.anchor: هائل لا يقادر قدره وقرأ جماعة

rows.speaker: جماعة من السبعة وابن عباس
rows.claim: A group among the Seven and Ibn ʿAbbās read the verb with fatḥa on yāʾ and ḥāʾ, using the Hijazi triliteral form; the Najdi and Tamimi dialect uses the quadriliteral form isḥāt.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جماعة من السبعة وابن عباس ( فيسحتكم ( بفتح الياء والحلق من الثلاثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning generalizes: whoever fabricates a lie against God, in any manner, has failed, especially the fabrication Moses forbids.
rows.anchor: كائنا من كان باى وجه كان فيدخل فيه الأفتراء المنهى عنه دخولا أوليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the failed fabricator is Pharaoh, and Moses warns the sorcerers not to share his failure and frustration.
rows.anchor: أو قد خاب فرعون المفترى فلا تكونوا مثله فى الخيبة وعدم نجح الطلبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause is parenthetical and reinforces the preceding warning.
rows.anchor: والجملة اعتراض مقرر لمضمون ما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative states the demand after the preceding argument; the explanatory fāʾ means: if matters are as described, resolve your plot together and act in unison.
rows.anchor: تصريح بالمطلوب إثر تمهيد المقدمات والفاء فصيحة أي إذا كان الأمر كما ذكر من كونهما ساحرين

rows.speaker: الزهري وابن محيصن وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وأبو حاتم
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī, Ibn Muḥayṣin, Abū ʿAmr, Yaʿqūb in one transmission, and Abū Ḥātim read with hamzat al-waṣl and fatḥa on mīm, meaning gather; 20:60's wording supports this reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهرى وابن محيصن وابو عمرو ويعقوب فى رواية وابو حاتم ( فاجمعوا ) بوصل الهمزة

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hishām says ajmaʿa applies only to abstract matters, while jamaʿa can refer to abstract matters or concrete things.
rows.anchor: قال ابن هشام : أن اجمع يتعلق بالمعانى فقط وجمع مشترك بين المعانى والذوات

rows.speaker: عمدة الحفاظ
rows.claim: ʿUmdat al-Ḥuffāẓ reports the view that ajmaʿa is mostly used for abstract matters and jamaʿa for concrete things, though usage can be reversed.
rows.anchor: وفى عمدة الحفاظ حكاية القول بأن اجمع اكثر ما يقال فى المعانى وجمع فى الأعيان

rows.speaker: المحكم
rows.claim: Al-Muḥkam treats the verbs alike: gathering an object from scattered parts is jamaʿa, and ajmaʿahu carries the same sense.
rows.anchor: وفى المحكم أنه يقال : جمع الشئ عن تفرقه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ distinguishes gathering scattered people, said with jamaʿtu, from gathering money, usually with a doubled jīm though it may be lightened; ijmāʿ can also mean resolve.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : إذا أردت جمع المتفرق قلت : جمعت القوم فهم مجموعون

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī distinguishes bringing things from different places from making them one whole.
rows.anchor: وقال العاصمعى : يقال جمعت الشئ إذا جئت به من هنا ومن هنا

rows.speaker: أبو الهيثم
rows.claim: Abū al-Haytham says assembling one's affair makes it one and resolves it after wavering.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الهيثم : أجمع أمره أي جعله جميعا وعزم عليه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses the verse under the first reading as: leave no part of your plot unused; bring it all forward.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : فى هذه الآية على القراءة الأولى أي لاتدعوا شيئا من كيدكم إلا جئتم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are told to come in rows because this is more intimidating to spectators and more effective at inspiring fear.
rows.anchor: أي مصتفين أمروا بذلك لأنه أهيب فى صدور الرائين وادخل فى استجلاب الرهبه من المشاهدين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Reports variously say the sorcerers numbered 70,000 with ropes and staffs, 72, 900, 15,000, or thirty-some thousand; one account divides the 900 among Persians, Romans, and Alexandrians.
rows.anchor: قيل : كانوا سبعين الف مع كل منهم حبل وعصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī says the reports' reliability is unclear and he is not inclined to the exaggerated totals.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى حال الاخبار فى ذلك والقلب لا يميل إلى المبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meeting place was probably spacious: Moses spoke from one part while the sorcerers deliberated elsewhere, then they were told to come to its center in formation.
rows.anchor: ولعل الموعد كان مكان متسعا خاطبهم موسى عليه السلام بما ذكر فى قطر من أقطاره

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda explains ṣaff as the place where people assemble for their festival and prayers.
rows.anchor: وقد فسر أبو عبيده الصف بالمكان الذى يجتمعون فيه لعيدهم وصلواتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī finds Abū ʿUbayda's explanation remote and suggests Ṣaff was a proper name for a specific place at the festival site; on that reading it is a direct object.
rows.anchor: وفيه بعد وكانه علم لموضع معين من مكان يوم الزينة
